module alu_seq #(
    parameter [7:0] p_key = 8'hAA   // Configurable internal security key (default 0xAA)
)(
    input i_clk,             // Clock signal
    input i_rst_b,           // Active-low asynchronous reset
    input [3:0] i_operand_a, // 4-bit input operand A
    input [3:0] i_operand_b, // 4-bit input operand B
    input [2:0] i_opcode,    // 3-bit operation code
    input [7:0] i_key_in,    // 8-bit security key input
    output reg [7:0] o_result // 8-bit operation result
);

    always @(posedge i_clk or negedge i_rst_b) begin
        if (!i_rst_b) begin
            // Active-low asynchronous reset initialises the output.
            o_result <= 8'b0;
        end else if (i_key_in == p_key) begin
            // Key matches: perform the requested operation.
            case (i_opcode)
                3'b000: o_result <= i_operand_a + i_operand_b; // Addition
                3'b001: o_result <= i_operand_a - i_operand_b; // Subtraction
                3'b010: o_result <= i_operand_a * i_operand_b; // Multiplication
                3'b011: o_result <= i_operand_a & i_operand_b; // Bitwise AND
                3'b100: o_result <= i_operand_a | i_operand_b; // Bitwise OR
                3'b101: o_result <= ~i_operand_a;              // Bitwise NOT of A
                3'b110: o_result <= i_operand_a ^ i_operand_b; // Bitwise XOR
                3'b111: o_result <= ~(i_operand_a ^ i_operand_b); // Bitwise XNOR
                default: o_result <= 8'b0;
            endcase
        end else begin
            // Key mismatch: no operation, output remains zero.
            o_result <= 8'b0;
        end
    end

endmodule

`timescale 1ns / 1ps

module sync_lifo #(
    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8,  // Width of the data
    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 3   // Number of bits for the address (determines the depth)
)(
    input wire clock,                         // System clock
    input wire reset,                         // Synchronous reset
    input wire write_en,                      // Write enable
    input wire read_en,                       // Read enable
    input wire [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] data_in,      // Data input to be written into LIFO
    output wire empty,                        // Indicates if LIFO is empty
    output wire full,                         // Indicates if LIFO is full
    output reg  error,                        // High on invalid op (read empty / write full)
    output reg  valid,                        // High when data_out holds valid data after a read
    output wire [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] data_out     // Data output from LIFO
);

    // Calculate depth of the LIFO using the address width
    localparam DEPTH = (1 << ADDR_WIDTH);      // Depth = 2^ADDR_WIDTH

    // Registers for LIFO logic
    reg [DEPTH-1:0] ptr;                       // Pointer for write/read operations
    reg [DEPTH-1:0] lifo_counter;              // Counter to track the number of elements in the LIFO
    reg [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] memory [DEPTH-1:0];   // Memory array to store LIFO data
    reg [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] temp_data_out;        // Temporary register for output data
    integer i;

    // Output assignments for empty and full flags
    assign empty = (lifo_counter == 0) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0;                  // LIFO is empty if counter is zero
    assign full  = (lifo_counter == DEPTH)? 1'b1 : 1'b0;               // LIFO is full if counter equals DEPTH

    // Counter logic to track the number of elements in LIFO
    always @(posedge clock) begin
        if (reset) begin
            lifo_counter <= 0;                                          // Reset the counter when reset signal is active
        end else if (!full && write_en) begin
            lifo_counter <= lifo_counter + 1;                           // Increment counter on write if LIFO is not full
        end else if (!empty && read_en) begin
            lifo_counter <= lifo_counter - 1;                           // Decrement counter on read if LIFO is not empty
        end
    end

    // Memory write logic: writes data into the LIFO
    always @(posedge clock) begin
        if (reset) begin
            ptr <= {ADDR_WIDTH {1'b0}};                                  // Reset pointer to zero on reset
        end else if (write_en && !full) begin
            memory[ptr] <= data_in;                                      // Write input data into memory at current pointer
            ptr <= ptr + 1;                                              // Increment pointer to next memory location
        end
    end

    // Memory read logic: reads data from the LIFO
    always @(posedge clock) begin
        if (reset) begin
            temp_data_out <= {DATA_WIDTH{1'b0}};                         // Clear output data on reset
        end else if (read_en && !empty) begin
            temp_data_out <= memory[ptr - 1'b1];                         // Read data from memory at (pointer - 1)
            ptr <= ptr - 1;                                              // Decrement pointer after reading
        end
    end

    // Registered error / valid flags, aligned with the registered data path
    // (a combinational flag would glitch one cycle early during a full<->empty
    //  transition while the enable is still asserted)
    always @(posedge clock) begin
        if (reset) begin
            error <= 1'b0;                                               // No error on reset
            valid <= 1'b0;                                               // No valid data on reset
        end else begin
            // error: write attempted while full (overflow) OR read attempted while empty (underflow)
            error <= (write_en && full) || (read_en && empty);
            // valid: high the cycle data_out holds the result of a successful read
            valid <= (read_en && !empty);
        end
    end

    // Assign the output data
    assign data_out = temp_data_out;                                     // Assign temp data output to the actual output
endmodule

`timescale 1ns / 1ps
module sync_serial_communication_tx_rx(
    input clk,                     // Clock signal
    input reset_n,                 // Active low reset signal
    input [2:0] sel,               // Selection signal for TX block
    input [63:0] data_in,          // 64-bit data input for TX block
    output [63:0] data_out,        // 64-bit data output from RX block
    output done,                   // Done signal indicating completion
    output parity_error            // Parity error flag for the communication link
);

// Internal signals
wire tx_out;                       // Serial data output from TX block
wire tx_done;                      // Done signal from TX block
wire serial_clk_in;                // Serial clock generated by TX block
wire parity_bit;                   // Parity bit generated by TX block

// Instantiate the TX block
tx_block uut_tx_block (
    .clk(clk),                     // Clock input to TX block
    .reset_n(reset_n),             // Reset input to TX block
    .data_in(data_in),             // 64-bit data input to TX block
    .sel(sel),                     // Selection signal to TX block
    .serial_out(tx_out),           // Serial data output from TX block
    .done(tx_done),                // Done signal from TX block
    .serial_clk(serial_clk_in),    // Serial clock output from TX block
    .parity(parity_bit)            // Parity bit output from TX block
);

// Instantiate the RX block
rx_block uut_rx_block (
    .clk(clk),                     // Clock input to RX block
    .serial_clk(serial_clk_in),    // Serial clock input to RX block
    .reset_n(reset_n),             // Reset input to RX block
    .sel(sel),                     // Selection signal to RX block
    .data_in(tx_out),              // Serial data input to RX block
    .parity_in(parity_bit),        // Parity bit input to RX block
    .data_out(data_out),           // 64-bit data output from RX block
    .done(done),                   // Done signal from RX block
    .parity_error(parity_error)    // Parity error output from RX block
);

endmodule

///// tx_block
module tx_block(
    input clk,               // Clock input
    input reset_n,           // Active-low reset input
    input [63:0] data_in,    // 64-bit parallel data input
    input [2:0] sel,         // Selection input to choose data width
    output reg serial_out,   // Serial data output
    output reg done,         // Done signal indicating completion of transmission
    output serial_clk,       // Clock for serial data transmission
    output reg parity        // Parity bit computed over the selected data
);

// Internal registers
reg [63:0] data_reg;         // Register to hold the data being transmitted
reg [6:0] bit_count;         // Counter to track number of bits to transmit
reg [6:0] reg_count;         // Register for counting bits for serial clock control
reg [6:0] temp_reg_count;    // Temporary register to track reg_count

// Compute the parity bit using the XOR reduction operator over the
// selected portion of data_in (transmitted alongside the serialized data).
always @(*) begin
    case (sel)
        3'b001:  parity = ^data_in[7:0];
        3'b010:  parity = ^data_in[15:0];
        3'b011:  parity = ^data_in[31:0];
        3'b100:  parity = ^data_in[63:0];
        default: parity = 1'b0;
    endcase
end

// Sequential block for state control and data selection
always @(posedge clk or negedge reset_n) begin
    if (!reset_n) begin
        // Reset all values on active-low reset
        data_reg     <= 64'h0;			     	           // Clear the data register
        bit_count    <= 7'h0;			     	           // Reset bit count to zero
        reg_count    <= 7'h0;		             	       // Reset reg_count to zero
    end else begin
        if (done == 1'b1) begin
	    // Case block to determine the width of data to transmit based on the 'sel' input
            case (sel)
                3'b000: begin
                    data_reg  <= 64'h0;             	   // No data selected
                    bit_count <= 7'd0;                     // No bits to transmit
                end
                3'b001: begin
                    data_reg  <= {56'h0, data_in[7:0]};    // Transmit lowest 8 bits
                    bit_count <= 7'd7;              	   // 8 bits to transmit
                end
                3'b010: begin
                    data_reg  <= {48'h0, data_in[15:0]};   // Transmit lowest 16 bits
                    bit_count <= 7'd15;             	   // 16 bits to transmit
                end
                3'b011: begin
                    data_reg  <= {32'h0, data_in[31:0]};   // Transmit lowest 32 bits
                    bit_count <= 7'd31;             	   // 32 bits to transmit
                end
                3'b100: begin
                    data_reg  <= data_in[63:0];     	   // Transmit all 64 bits
                    bit_count <= 7'd63;             	   // 64 bits to transmit
                end
                default: begin
                    data_reg  <= 64'h0;             	   // Default case: no data
                    bit_count <= 7'h0;              	   // No bits to transmit
                end
            endcase

        end else if (bit_count > 7'h0) begin
            data_reg   <= data_reg >> 1;                   // Shift the data to the right
            bit_count  <= bit_count - 1'b1;                // Decrement the bit count

        end
        reg_count <= bit_count;                            // Update reg_count for serial clock control
    end
end

// Generate serial clock based on reg_count
//`ifdef SIMULATION
assign  #1 serial_clk = clk && (temp_reg_count !== 7'd0) ;  // To avoid SImulator issue
//`else
//assign  serial_clk = clk && (temp_reg_count !== 7'd0) ;
//`endif

// Register to keep track of reg_count and use for clock gating
always@(posedge clk or negedge reset_n) begin
    if(!reset_n) begin
        temp_reg_count <= 7'h0;					           // Reset temporary reg_count
    end
    else begin
        temp_reg_count <= reg_count;			           // Update temp_reg_count with current reg_count
    end
end


// Sequential logic to drive the serial_out signal based on reg_count and bit_count
always@(posedge clk or negedge reset_n) begin
    if(!reset_n) begin
	   serial_out <= 1'b0;				                  // Reset serial output
    end
    else if(reg_count > 7'h0 || bit_count > 7'h0) begin
	   serial_out <= data_reg[0];			              // Output the least significant bit of data_reg
    end
end

// Set the done signal when transmission is complete (bit_count reaches zero)
always@(posedge clk or negedge reset_n) begin
    if(!reset_n) begin
        done <= 1'b0;					                  // Reset done output
    end
    else begin
     if(bit_count == 7'h0) begin
	    done <= 1'b1; 			                          // Set done signal high when transmission is done
     end
     else begin
	    done <= 1'b0;					                  // Clear done signal during transmission
     end
end
end


endmodule

///// rx_block
module rx_block(
    input wire clk,  			    // clock input
    input wire reset_n,			    // Active-low reset
    input wire data_in,			    // Serial input data
    input wire serial_clk,		    // Clock signal for serial data
    input wire [2:0] sel,           // Selection output to choose data width
    input wire parity_in,           // Parity bit received from the TX block
    output reg done,			    // Done signal to indicate data reception complete
    output reg [63:0] data_out, 	// Parallel output data after serial operation
    output reg parity_error         // High when the received parity does not match

);

    // Internal registers
    reg [63:0] data_reg;		    // Register to hold incoming serial data
    reg [7:0] bit_count;		    // Counter for the number of bits received
    reg [7:0] count;			    // General purpose counter to sync with bit_count


    // Sequential logic block to capture serial data on the rising edge of serial_clk
    always @(posedge serial_clk or negedge  reset_n) begin
        if (!reset_n) begin		    // Reset all registers on reset_n (active low)
            data_reg <= 64'h0;		// Clear the data register
            bit_count <= 8'd0;		// Clear the bit counter
        end else begin
            if(done == 1'b1) begin                   // If done signal is asserted, reset the bit counter and data register
                bit_count <= 8'b0;
                data_reg <= 64'h0;
            end
            else begin
                 bit_count <= bit_count;			 // Maintain the bit counter if not done
            end
                bit_count <= bit_count + 1'b1;	     // Increment bit count
                data_reg[bit_count]<=data_in; 	     // Store the incoming data bit
           end
    end

    // Sequential logic block to monitor the completion of data reception and update outputs
    always@(posedge clk or negedge reset_n) begin
    	if(!reset_n) begin			 	             // Reset all registers on reset_n (active low)
    	   count <= 8'd0;					         // Clear the bit counter
           done <= 1'b0;					         // Deassert done signal
           data_out <= 64'h0;					     // Clear the output data register
           parity_error <= 1'b0;                     // Clear the parity error flag
        end
        else if(count >= bit_count && count != 8'd0) begin       // When the count reaches the bit_count, assert done and output the data
           done <= 1'b1;				             // Set done to indicate transmission complete
           // Validate the received parity against the computed parity of the
           // reconstructed data: HIGH when they differ, LOW when they match.
           parity_error <= (parity_in != (^data_reg));
           case(sel)
            3'b000:begin
                data_out <= 64'h0;                   // no bits to transmit
            end
            3'b001:begin
                data_out <= {56'h0,data_reg};        // 8 bits of data_reg
            end
            3'b010:begin
                data_out <= {48'h0,data_reg};        // 16 bits of data_reg
            end
            3'b011:begin
                data_out <= {32'h0,data_reg};        // 32 bits of data_reg
            end
            3'b100:begin
                data_out <= data_reg;                // 64 bits of data_reg
            end
            default:begin
                data_out <= 64'h0;                   // no bits to transmit, default state
            end
           endcase
        end
        else if(bit_count > 8'd0) begin              // If bits are being received, increment the count and deassert done
           count <= count+ 1'b1;				     // Increment count
           done <= 1'b0;					         // Clear done signal while receiving
           parity_error <= 1'b0;                     // No parity result while still receiving
        end
        else begin  			                     // If no bits have been received, reset the count and deassert done
           count <= 8'd0;					         // Reset count
           done <= 1'b0;					         // Clear done signal
           parity_error <= 1'b0;                     // Clear the parity error flag
        end
    end

endmodule
